prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations(typical durations unless Handling Resource Planner/stand constraint), Adverse Weather(bus/loader/tow padded), Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved shorter cycles; no pushback surges), Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Actors: Regional Flow Manager, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor(monitors release rate vs spacing/runway crossings), Airport Duty Manager, Ramp Control Lead(reviews pushback windows vs apron congestion/towing/readiness before accepting), Aircraft Operator Representative; Halcyon records pushback-window rationale in coordination notes before release. Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell: normalizes Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan; proposes TOBT; TOBT conditional if resources late; locks at freeze horizon unless exception/override; separates ATC vs handling delay; logs alerts/acks/decisions in Audit Event Ledger. Parts: Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone(demand profile by stand/apron/runway/fix; flags imbalancing TOBTs); Capacity Assessment Module(compares demand vs Airport Acceptance Rate, runway config, taxiway, sector limits; late reduction recalculates AAR; restriction=time-bounded throughput cut); Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(CTT; priority emergency/national>scheduled>GA; shall adjust times when metering needs stand absorption; revises only within authority+fairness); Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove(value/confidence/reason code; feasibility→Saffron, AOR; restriction status/notes→Common Situation Display); Departure Metering Service=Emberline(runway demand→stand delay; derives TOBT protecting CTT without surface overload; stand absorption preferred if no gate conflict; pushback windows=narrow bands, not clearance; CTT→Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf, refresh advisories on restriction change; Business Rules Registry spacing); North/South Runway Meter(independent queue counts); Surface Surveillance Adapter(confirms holding-point queues); East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board=Skylark(produces Fuel Truck Hold Advice); Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard(→CAM); Flight Data Exchange(intent→DMS); Airline Interface Adapter; Time Synchronization Service; Performance Analytics Warehouse(compares planned capacity, alerts, acks, realized delay); Collaborative Decision Log; Identity Access Service; Alert Distribution

New part:
S362: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether each affected aircraft can absorb the assigned delay at stand without compromising crew, passenger, or turnaround constraints.
S363: If an operator cannot accept the proposed stand delay, the Aircraft Operator Representative requests reconsideration through the Airport CDM Portal.
S364: The Gate Conflict Detector warns when continued stand holding would block an inbound allocation or create a conflict with a planned equipment move.
S365: Business Rules Registry parameters define the maximum planned runway queue, the warning threshold, and the intervention threshold for each runway configuration.
S366: When a predicted queue exceeds the warning threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub highlights the affected runway queue on the Common Situation Display.
S367: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Regional Flow Manager may increase stand absorption to prevent unstable taxi queues from forming under reduced visibility or wet surface conditions.
S368: In a Capacity Reduction State, the Airport Duty Manager and Tower Supervisor agree whether the metering horizon should be extended so that delay is absorbed before pushback rather than near the runway.
S369: All changes to Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, and threshold overrides are written to the Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger.
S370: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned stand absorption, actual off block performance, and runway queue length to verify that the agreed thresholds were not exceeded.
S371: The Regional Flow Platform enters the winter operating mode when freezing precipitation, contamination reports, or low surface temperature forecasts make untreated ground movement unreliable.
S372: The Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms the trigger conditions in the Digital Briefing Room so that airport, airline, and tower participants share one operational assumption.
S373: In this mode, the Capacity Assessment Module reduces practical departure capacity to account for deicing time, pad transit time, and slower ramp taxi speeds.
S374: The Airport Capacity Plan is revised with a winter margin before the Slot Allocation Engine recalculates affected Calculated Takeoff Time values.
S375: The Deicing Coordinator maintains the active pad configuration, including open bays, closed bays, fluid limitations, and vehicle availability.
S376: Pad queue controls assign aircraft to a deicing lane only after the Target Off Block Time is stable enough to support a realistic treatment sequence.
S377: The Ramp Movement Board displays each aircraft as pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, or returning to stand when treatment cannot be completed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
